subject: a nightly batch pipeline that cleans order exports and writes them for reporting
conclusion: orderflow reads the day's exports, sends bad rows to quarantine, drops duplicates, adds the region and writes JSON Lines.
why: A bad row never stops the run. The quarantine file keeps each rejected row with its reason, so a person can fix the source.

glossary.definition: a file that keeps rejected rows with the reason they failed
a text file with one JSON object on each line

flow.title: One nightly run
flow.text: A staged process with one branch: rows that fail a check leave the main path for quarantine.

items.label: Ingest
items.desc: The ingest step reads every CSV export for the date, row by row.

items.label: Validate
items.desc: Each row passes every check or gets the first reason it failed.

items.label: Quarantine
items.desc: A failed row goes to the quarantine file with its reason and its source file.

items.label: Dedupe
items.desc: The dedupe step keeps the first copy of each order and counts the rest.

items.label: Enrich
items.desc: The enrich step adds the customer's region from a lookup file.

items.label: Load
items.desc: The load step writes the clean rows as one JSON Lines file per date.

facts.text: An amount of zero or less sends the row to quarantine.
The load step writes to a temporary file and then renames it, so a reader never sees half a file.

inferred: A rerun for the same date replaces that date's output instead of adding to it.

lines.name: read
lines.text: The run reads every export for the date.

lines.name: check
lines.text: Each row passes the checks, or it goes to quarantine with a reason.

lines.name: clean
lines.text: Good rows lose their duplicates, gain a region and land in one file.

lines.name: counts
lines.text: The run reports how many rows it wrote and how many it rejected.

lines.name: duplicates
lines.text: It also counts the duplicate orders it dropped.
